briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Middle East saw a significant escalation in US-Iran tensions over the past 24 hours, marked by reciprocal strikes between the two powers and Iranian attacks on US military installations in Bahrain and Kuwait. Concurrently, Israel and Lebanon signed a US-brokered framework agreement aimed at de-escalating the northern border, though it faces strong opposition from Hezbollah and internal Israeli disagreement.

IRAN
US forces conducted additional airstrikes against Iranian military surveillance infrastructure, communication systems, air defense sites, drone storage facilities, and minelayer capabilities in the Strait of Hormuz area, specifically targeting Sirik, Qeshm Island, Bandar Lengeh, and Bandar Kong. These strikes were in response to an Iranian drone attack on the Panamanian-flagged oil tanker MT Kiku in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran’s Islamic Revolution Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy and Aerospace Forces claimed responsibility for a "decisive response," launching ballistic missiles and drones between 02:00 and 03:00 AM on June 28, targeting eight key US military installations, including Ali Al-Salem Air Base in Kuwait and the Fifth Fleet naval base in Salman Port, Bahrain, claiming their destruction. Iranian state media reported several projectiles struck a telecommunications tower near Sirik. US and Bahraini forces reported shooting down 9 Iranian one-way attack drones with no damage or injuries. Kuwaiti air defenses also reportedly intercepted missiles and drones.

Politically, members of the Assembly of Experts issued a statement on negotiations, emphasizing adherence to red lines and calling for the "punishment" of US President Trump and Israeli PM Netanyahu for past actions. The IRGC asserted that violating the ceasefire, which they accuse the US of doing, would lead to a complete halt of all diplomatic processes. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi is slated to visit Iraq, and he also expressed condolences and offered aid to Venezuela following recent earthquakes. Iran’s government spokeswoman Fatemeh Mohajerani stated that Iran and Oman will consult on administering the Strait of Hormuz. Internally, a debate persists regarding the establishment of a communication line with the US, with an IRGC spokesperson denying it while a security source confirmed it as purely political.

ISRAEL
The Israeli military announced the killing of Walid Haniyeh, deputy commander of a Hamas Nukhba Force company and nephew of former Hamas political leader Ismail Haniyeh, in Gaza. He was reportedly involved in the October 7, 2023 infiltration into Israel. Israeli forces also conducted a drone strike in Al-Nabatiya, southern Lebanon, reportedly injuring at least one Lebanese civilian.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu held a press conference, announcing his intention to form a "broad national government" and describing the newly signed framework agreement with Lebanon as a "major blow to Iran and Hezbollah." Defense Minister Israel Katz hailed the "historic" deal, stating that the IDF would not entirely withdraw from Lebanon but would maintain a security zone, including the Beaufort Castle ridge area, and prepare for a "prolonged stay" until Hezbollah is disarmed. Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich also welcomed the agreement as a significant achievement. However, National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir strongly criticized the agreement, calling it a "big mistake" and requesting a cabinet vote, arguing that Lebanon would not disarm Hezbollah. Former Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the "Yashar" party, criticized Netanyahu's leadership, accusing him of division and inciting draft evasion.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Israeli forces killed Walid Haniyeh, a senior Hamas Nukhba Force commander, in Gaza. The Gaza Health Ministry reported eight Palestinians killed and 20 wounded in Israeli military offensives across the Gaza Strip over the past 24 hours. Israeli forces carried out an airstrike targeting a Palestinian farm and agricultural land in Deir al-Balah, central Gaza. An Israeli drone strike on a tent near the Dabit junction in Gaza City reportedly injured at least 22 Palestinians, including several children. In the West Bank, the core families of a new settlement called Noa, located in northern Samaria, arrived in the area for the first time.

LEBANON
Israel and Lebanon signed a US-mediated framework agreement in Washington. Key details include Israel's commitment to gradually withdraw the IDF from areas in southern Lebanon (with Zouter West and Froun identified as initial pilot areas) contingent on Hezbollah’s disarmament. Israel stated it would maintain a security zone and has no territorial ambitions in Lebanon, while Lebanon would assume security responsibility.
Hezbollah’s Secretary-General Naim Qassem strongly rejected the agreement, labeling it "null and void," a "terrible mistake," and an act that legalizes Israeli occupation and sacrifices Lebanese sovereignty. Mohammad Raad, head of Hezbollah’s parliamentary bloc, echoed this, criticizing the Lebanese authority's stance. The Ansarullah movement in Yemen also viewed the agreement as a plot to "destroy resistance." US President Trump congratulated Lebanese President Joseph Aoun on signing the agreement. France and Italy have expressed readiness to offer diplomatic support for the agreement. Separately, Lebanese media reported Israeli drone strikes in Al-Nabatiya, southern Lebanon, causing at least one injury. The Lebanese judiciary reportedly called on security forces to address protests and roadblocks against the agreement.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Baghdad experienced significant security activity, with reports of extensive gunfire and heavy military deployments, including Abrams tanks, in the Green Zone. Iraqi anti-terrorism forces, special divisions, and the 9th Armored Division were deployed for operations that led to the arrest of at least eight senior political officials on corruption charges. Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi announced that US-led coalition forces would withdraw from Iraq by September. Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi is scheduled to visit Iraq tomorrow for bilateral and regional discussions. There was an unconfirmed report of a drone strike on a camp of Kurdish-Iranian opposition forces in northern Iraq and an unconfirmed report of an assassination attempt targeting a Kurdish opposition leader in a hotel in Erbil.

GULF STATES
Bahrain and Kuwait reported being targeted by Iranian ballistic missiles and drones, with air raid sirens activated in both countries. Bahrain's Ministry of Interior urged citizens to remain calm and seek safe places, while Kuwait's Ministry of Defense confirmed its air defenses were engaging "hostile missile and drone attacks." US officials confirmed that US and Bahraini forces intercepted nine Iranian one-way attack drones aimed at US forces in Bahrain, with no reported damage or injuries. Bahrain, Kuwait, UAE, and Qatar issued condemnations of Iran's attacks, characterizing them as violations of sovereignty and international law, threats to security, and destabilizing actions that undermine peace efforts. The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) raised the security threat level in the Strait of Hormuz to "Substantial" following renewed attacks on merchant vessels, warning of naval mines and increased naval presence. Iran's IRGC Navy declared its control over traffic arrangements in the Strait of Hormuz and warned of a "stronger response" to "violating ships." Iran's government spokeswoman also mentioned that Iran and Oman would engage in consultations to determine a framework for managing the Strait of Hormuz.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **US-Iran Direct Military Exchanges:** The US launched renewed airstrikes on Iranian military targets in the Strait of Hormuz area (Sirik, Qeshm, Bandar Lengeh, Bandar Kong) in response to an Iranian drone attack on the MT Kiku oil tanker.
2.  **Iranian Retaliation on US Bases:** Iran's IRGC launched ballistic missiles and drones targeting US military installations at Ali Al-Salem Air Base in Kuwait and the Fifth Fleet naval base in Salman Port, Bahrain. US and Bahraini forces intercepted nine Iranian drones, with no reported damage or casualties.
3.  **Lebanon-Israel Framework Agreement:** Israel and Lebanon signed a US-brokered framework agreement, with Israel committing to a phased withdrawal from southern Lebanon contingent on Hezbollah's disarmament, while maintaining a security zone.
4.  **Hezbollah Rejection of Agreement:** Hezbollah's Secretary-General Naim Qassem and other party officials strongly condemned the Lebanon-Israel agreement as illegitimate and a betrayal of Lebanese sovereignty.
5.  **Iraqi Political Purge:** Extensive security operations in Baghdad's Green Zone led to the arrest of at least eight senior political officials on corruption charges, accompanied by heavy military deployment.
6.  **Trump's Ultimatum to Iran:** US President Trump issued a stark warning, stating that "If Iran continues to violate the ceasefire, the Islamic Republic of Iran will cease to exist," indicating a potential for further military action.
7.  **Iranian Condemnation by Gulf States:** Bahrain, Kuwait, UAE, and Qatar condemned Iran's attacks on Bahrain and Kuwait as violations of sovereignty and international law.
8.  **Hamas Commander Eliminated:** The IDF killed Walid Haniyeh, a senior Hamas Nukhba Force commander and nephew of Ismail Haniyeh, in Gaza.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are critically high due to direct military exchanges between the US and Iran, coupled with Iran's expansion of targets to US military installations in Gulf states. President Trump's explicit threat that "the Islamic Republic of Iran will cease to exist" indicates a severe potential for a broader conflict. Active flashpoints include the Strait of Hormuz, where maritime attacks and military responses continue, and Southern Lebanon, where Israeli strikes persist amidst Hezbollah's strong rejection of the new agreement. The ongoing Israeli operations in the Gaza Strip also remain a source of instability. Military postures have intensified, with the US conducting larger-scope strikes, Iran explicitly targeting US bases, and Israel maintaining a "security zone" in Lebanon. The UKMTO has raised the security threat level in the Strait of Hormuz to "Substantial," signaling increased risk to commercial shipping. Red lines include US expectations for Iran to adhere to ceasefire agreements and refrain from attacking commercial shipping and US forces, while Iran views US strikes on its territory and any violations of the Islamabad MoU as red lines. Furthermore, elements within Iran's Assembly of Experts have called for the assassination of Trump and Netanyahu if perceived red lines are crossed.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **US** has intensified its posture, conducting renewed and larger-scale strikes against Iranian targets in the Strait of Hormuz region. President Trump issued a strong warning about Iran's continued existence. US Vice President Vance expressed optimism about ongoing talks with Iran. **Bahrain, Kuwait, the UAE, and Qatar** have unequivocally condemned Iran's drone attacks on Bahrain and Kuwait, viewing them as severe violations of national sovereignty, threats to regional security, and destabilizing actions that undermine peace efforts. **Oman** is engaged in discussions with Iran regarding the administration of the Strait of Hormuz. In **Lebanon**, President Joseph Aoun received congratulations from President Trump on signing the framework agreement with Israel, but Hezbollah leaders, including Secretary-General Naim Qassem, vehemently rejected the deal. The Lebanese judiciary has called for security forces to address protests against the agreement. **France and Italy** expressed diplomatic support for the Lebanon-Israel agreement. **Iraq** saw its Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi announce the withdrawal of US-led coalition forces by September, amidst internal security operations. **Pakistan**, which mediated the Islamabad MoU, held discussions on West Asia developments with the UK Foreign Minister. No specific statements or actions from Russia, China, or Turkey were reported in the provided messages.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Contradictions persist regarding the nature of US-Iran communication. An IRGC spokesperson denied a direct communication line in the Strait of Hormuz, while an Iranian security source confirmed a purely political, non-military channel, suggesting internal disagreement or differing narratives. Israeli statements on troop withdrawal from Lebanon are nuanced; Netanyahu and Katz insist on maintaining a security zone until Hezbollah's disarmament, contrasting with some summaries suggesting a full withdrawal. Unverified claims include reports of an assassination attempt on a Kurdish opposition leader in Erbil and specific details of damage to US bases in Kuwait and Bahrain by Iranian strikes, which are not corroborated by US/Bahraini reports of drone interceptions without damage. Propaganda is evident in both Iranian and Israeli messaging, with Iran framing its actions as a "decisive response" and asserting "dominance," while Israeli leaders portray the Lebanon agreement as a "historic blow" to Iran/Hezbollah. Omid Dana's channel frequently contains highly opinionated, anti-regime content, serving more as an indicator of internal dissent and counter-narratives than factual reporting. Reporting gaps remain on the precise extent of damage to Iranian military targets from US strikes and the full operational details and timelines of the Lebanon-Israel framework agreement.
